title: StatisticalVariable
description: A reusable definition of what is measured, independent of any source: 'Population age 65+', 'Median household income'. This is schema.org `StatisticalVariable`. A source's own code (a census table cell, a national-statistics series ID) is a mapping, not the identifier: it goes in a crosswalk, or in `identifier` with its scheme named.

@id.description: This variable's own dereferenceable identifier. Never a source's code.

description.description: What exactly is counted or calculated, including the universe it covers (people, households, occupied housing units).

populationType.description: The kind of thing counted, as a schema.org class: `Person`. Optional, because schema.org has no class for every universe (households, for one).

measuredProperty.description: The property measured, as an IRI from any vocabulary. Optional.

measurementDenominator.description: For a rate or share, the `StatisticalVariable` it is a share of.

additionalProperty.description: The dimensions that define this subset of the population, one `PropertyValue` each. Age 65 and over is `{propertyID: age, minValue: 65, unitText: year}`; female is `{propertyID: gender, value: Female}`. Use `value` for a category and `minValue`/`maxValue` for a range. schemaGov defines no dimension vocabulary: publishers reuse the same `propertyID` for the same dimension.

identifier.description: Scheme-qualified identifiers for this variable in other systems.

sameAs.description: The same variable defined elsewhere, such as a Data Commons or SDMX definition.
